findings.title: Queries are interpolated more than once, so ad-hoc filters can be appended repeatedly
findings.body:
`runSplitQuery` now calls `applyTemplateVariables` on every target. In the sharding path, `runShardSplitQuery` (shardQuerySplitting.ts:52) has already called `applyTemplateVariables`. It then passes a sub-request that still carries `request.filters` into `runSplitQuery`, which applies it a second time.

The sub-requests also go through `datasource.runQuery`. If that ends up in `DataSourceWithBackend.query`, it calls `applyTemplateVariables` per target again, which would make a third pass.

`applyTemplateVariables` is not idempotent. It injects ad-hoc filter matchers from `request.filters` into the expression, so those label matchers can be duplicated. Values containing `$` or regex-escaped multi-value variables can also be re-processed and corrupted.

The new shard test asserts 5 calls for a single target, which reflects this repeated application. Interpolation should happen exactly once: drop it from one entry point, or strip `filters`/`scopedVars` from the request after interpolating.

findings.title: Mocked applyTemplateVariables mutates input and hides double-interpolation effects
findings.body:
The mock replaces `$SELECTOR` in place and returns the same object. Applying it a second time is therefore a no-op. Because of that, the tests cannot detect the duplicated filter/escaping problem caused by calling `applyTemplateVariables` several times per query.

The mock also mutates `request.targets`, which a non-mutating real implementation would not do. A test with ad-hoc filters that asserts the final expression contains each filter only once would catch the regression.
